World.title: No mercy for corrupt officials as Al-Zaidi widens Iraq crackdown
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s anti-corruption effort has shown no signs of stopping, with arrests and investigations ranging from senior Oil Ministry officials to MPs, former provincial leaders, and other government figures since he assumed office.

One of the main early instances involved Adnan Al-Jumaili, the former deputy oil minister for refining affairs, whose imprisonment was a key development in the probe.

Statements gathered from Al-Jumaili assisted authorities in expanding their investigation into a larger network of politicians and officials accused of profiting from government contracts and state resources.

That probe culminated in a spectacular operation on June 28, when Iraqi security forces blocked off access to Baghdad’s highly defended Green Zone and conducted coordinated raids on political and government heavyweights.

Iraq’s national news agency first claimed 47 arrests, including 12 current parliamentarians, a former legislator, a former aide to former Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, and a top Oil Ministry official.

According to sources inside Iraq’s anti-corruption authorities, there were 67 people held during the first phase of the “Dawn Crackdown”.

Ali Maarij, Iraq’s Deputy Oil Minister for distribution and another key player in the country’s energy industry, was among those held.

According to prosecutors, the larger investigation turned up claims of the misuse of public resources, government contracts, and commissions for personal or political gain.

Authorities also recovered a considerable quantity of assets related to the investigations. Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council said in July that 375 kg of gold had been confiscated as part of the al-Jumaili probe, with more cash and gold found in subsequent operations.

Instead of finishing with the first Green Zone attacks, the campaign lasted all of July.

Between July 20 and July 26, Iraqi police apprehended 31 persons in seven corruption cases, reflecting the government’s escalating enforcement campaign.

So far, August has delivered a slew of high-profile cases.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, was held as authorities investigated claims involving public finances, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court for a separate inquiry.

On Sunday, police detained Hashem al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company, on suspicion of corruption regarding a Ministry of Defense contract.

The specifics of the alleged infractions and the contract’s worth have not yet been released.

The financial impact of the crackdown is becoming significant.

The Eco Iraq Observatory said on Sunday that police had recovered around 482.6 billion Iraqi dinars ($371.6 million) in stolen assets, including cash and gold.

Taken together, the arrests convey an increasingly clear message from Al-Zaidi’s government: senior political ties, legislative standing, or positions inside major ministries should not exclude people from scrutiny.

However, arrests alone will not decide whether Iraq eventually succeeds in combating corruption.

Success will be predicated on transforming the present campaign into long-term institutional transformation via open government contracts, improved audits, digital financial systems, independent investigations, and tighter controls over public funds.

This is especially crucial as Iraq pursues tens of billions of dollars in foreign investment and works to strengthen economic ties with the United States, Europe, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and other Gulf nations.

Investors need to be confident that predictable rules govern contracts and public institutions rather than political interference.

The crackdown has also received backing from key international partners.

During a phone call with French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday, Macron reaffirmed France’s support for Iraq’s anti-corruption drive and economic reforms, as well as continued cooperation on counterterrorism and strengthening the capabilities of the Iraqi armed forces.

But the problem goes beyond financial corruption.

Al-Zaidi has committed to reinforce state power and bring armaments under government control, adding to the administration’s already arduous task of dealing with entrenched political and economic interests.

Iraq’s long-term goal must consequently be greater than capturing people.

Baghdad needs institutions strong enough to prevent corruption and foreign intervention from resurfacing under new political networks, whether sponsored by Iran or another external entity.

If Al-Zaidi can combine rigorous enforcement with due process and institutional change, the campaign might greatly boost trust in the Iraqi government.

Without such institutional improvements, even hundreds of arrests risk becoming a momentary crackdown rather than the long-term transformation Iraq requires.

World.title: Iraq opens its first IMAX cinema in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated its first IMAX theater at the Iraq Mall in Baghdad, introducing the premium large-screen movie format to the nation for the first time.

Sarwa Abdul Wahid, the Acting Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities, formally opened the new Iraqi Cinema branch in the mall, adding to Baghdad’s fast expanding entertainment and leisure sector.

According to IMAX’s official listing, the Iraq Mall site in Baghdad has an IMAX with Laser auditorium and stadium seating.

The launch allows Iraqi consumers to see important worldwide movies in IMAX without having to fly abroad, like Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey.

The film, starring Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Robert Pattinson, and Lupita Nyong’o, was the first feature film filmed exclusively on IMAX film cameras.

The Odyssey has also emerged as one of 2026’s greatest box office triumphs, earning more over $260 million globally in its first weekend.

Iraqi Cinema is now offering daily IMAX screenings of the film at its Iraq Mall location.

IMAX brings another worldwide entertainment option to Baghdad, as Iraq seeks additional investment in retail malls, restaurants, hotels, theaters, and other leisure developments, while also growing its domestic tourist and entertainment sectors.

World.title: Iraq arrests senior Trade Ministry official Hashem Al-Sudani
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi prosecutors detained Hashem Al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company (GAMCO), on Sunday for suspected embezzlement in a contract with the Ministry of Defense.

The contract’s specifics, including its value and the particular alleged infractions under investigation, have not been released. Al-Sudani’s arrest is part of Iraq’s growing anti-corruption effort, which targets prominent government officials, legislators, and business leaders.

The new arrest comes as Baghdad ramps up the “Dawn Crackdown,” an anti-corruption operation that began on June 28 by Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to probe big crimes involving public contracts and state finances.

The initiative has gained traction among senior and politically connected individuals.

Recently, police arrested former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court as part of a separate inquiry.

Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and reclaiming public monies, with authorities attempting to show that probes would extend to officials regardless of party or institutional affiliation.

Corruption has long been a major impediment to Iraq’s growth, depleting state resources, degrading public services, and deterring private and international investment.

The ongoing arrests imply Baghdad’s new effort is spreading to official institutions, but anyone arrested or interrogated has not been convicted and is still subject to due process.

World.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Belgorod region.

The World Health Organization denounced a strike that destroyed a warehouse in Ukraine holding medical supplies.

More than four years after the start of Russia’s large-scale offensive against Ukraine, both countries are ramping up long-range strikes. The resulting civilian casualties led the United Nations to condemn both sides last week.

Russia is relying on “ballistic terror,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at Ukraine this week.

“More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed,” he added.

The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, said Zelensky.

Twenty-three people were also wounded, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov, sharing images of a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene.

Zelensky said eight people had also been wounded overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings.

He condemned another “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region that wounded nine people, including four children.

– WHO condemns warehouse strike –

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a WHO warehouse stocking medical supplies in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro had been destroyed in strikes on Friday.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros in a post on X Sunday.

“Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!”

In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region’s acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev.

Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also wounded, he added.

Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, said Shuvaev.

A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street.

On the front line, the Russian army said Sunday they had captured two small villages in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region. The claim has not yet been independently verified.

One of them, Vasiutynske, is about 10 kilometres (six miles) from the city of Kramatorsk, a Ukrainian urban and logistical hub.

– Zelensky defends strikes –

Zelensky, in his evening address on Sunday, defended Ukraine’s responses to Russia’s attacks — including strikes on oil refineries, air-defence systems and radar stations — as “truly just responses”.

“The Russian war will be increasingly felt at home, in Russia,” he said.

On Thursday, United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemned both sides for their repeated attacks on civilian areas.

“Attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are a clear violation of international humanitarian law, and must stop immediately,” he said.

The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled.

World.title: Como sign England defender Chalobah from Chelsea
World.content:
Milan – Como have completed the signing of England centre-back Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea for a reported fee of 30 million euros ($34.5 million), the Serie A club announced Sunday.

The 27-year-old has penned a five-year deal with Cesc Fabregas’s ambitious side, who will play in the Champions League for the first time this season.

“I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans,” said Chalobah, who made 151 appearances for Chelsea.

“I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together.”

Como pipped AC Milan and Juventus to Italy’s fourth and final Champions League place last season.

Scudetto holders Inter Milan had also been heavily linked with a move for Chalobah, before reportedly deciding the asking price was too high.

“Trevoh is an important signing for us and a player who represents the level of ambition we have at this club,” said Como coach Fabregas, a former Chelsea midfielder.

“He is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Chalobah was part of the England squad which finished third at the World Cup last month, after receiving a late call-up as a replacement for the injured Tino Livramento.

He could make his Como debut when they visit Udinese in their Serie A opener on August 22.

World.title: Iraq steps up digital transformation of banking and customs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is speeding up preparations to digitize its financial and customs systems, with Finance Minister Falih Sari and Central Bank Governor Nizar Nasser Hussein considering tighter integration of electronic payments, customs processes, and government financial data.

The conference, which included members from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), aimed to accelerate electronic linkages between Iraq’s customs and payment systems.

Sari urged authorities to speed up implementation as part of measures to modernize financial management, streamline trade processes, and create a more efficient environment for companies and investors.

The talks also focused on increasing cooperation between fiscal and monetary agencies, including digital data interchange and upgrading Iraq’s banking infrastructure, while maintaining financial stability and meeting government financial responsibilities.

The revisions are part of Iraq’s larger transition from cash-heavy and paper-based institutions to a more integrated digital financial infrastructure.

Baghdad sees modernization of banking, payments, and customs as more crucial as the government strives to bring its financial system closer to international norms, increase transparency, and make it simpler for Iraqi and foreign enterprises to do business.

The drive also supports broader banking changes in Iraq, as the government seeks deeper connectivity with the international financial system and encourages private sector development.

World.title: PSG sign France full-back Digne from Villa
World.content:
Paris – Aston Villa left-back Lucas Digne has joined Paris Saint-Germain on a three-year deal, the European champions announced Sunday.

The 33-year-old French international, who grew up in the Paris region, returns to PSG, where he played for two seasons between 2013 and 2015.

“I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain,” Digne said in a statement on the Ligue 1 champions’ website.

“I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years.

“I can’t wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team.”

After PSG, Digne spent time on loan in Serie A with Roma before signing for Spanish giants Barcelona, who were then coached by current PSG boss Luis Enrique.

He moved to the Premier League in 2018, firstly with Everton, then four years later joining Aston Villa.

At Villa Park, he won the Europa League under Unai Emery last season.

Capped 64 times by his country, Digne became France’s first-choice left-back over the course of the 2026 World Cup.

Digne is PSG’s second major signing of the summer transfer window after fellow French international Maghnes Akliouche arrived from Monaco.

He could make his debut for his new club against his former employers Aston Villa on Wednesday in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg.

However, long term it is likely his principal role will be to provide cover for PSG’s starting left-back, Nuno Mendes.

World.title: Former Iraq finance minister Taif Sami summoned in widening corruption probe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami has been officially summoned by a court and put on a judicial wanted list as authorities broaden a corruption probe that has reached high political and government officials, according to sources.

Sami is thought to be outside Iraq and has not been captured.

The alleged court action is part of an inquiry and does not prove misconduct or lead to a conviction.

The revelation comes as Iraq’s new administration steps up its anti-corruption effort, which has already resulted in the detention of important political personalities and bureaucrats.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, often known as Abu Mazen, was detained in Baghdad recently on suspicions of misusing public contract funds.

A close acquaintance was also arrested as part of the inquiry.

The new charges stem from a big operation in Baghdad’s highly protected Green Zone in late June, when Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service detained numerous officials as part of a larger corruption probe.

According to reports at the time, authorities were looking into claims involving government contracts and huge sums of public money.

Sami, the previous administration’s finance minister under former Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammad Shia Al-Sudani, was one of Iraq’s most significant economic leaders, responsible for handling the federal budget, government expenditures, and financial ties between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

The purported summons therefore implies a potentially major extension of the probe against individuals who formerly held top positions inside the Iraqi state.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and improving state institutions as part of its domestic agenda to boost public trust and reassure international investors.

With the arrest of Abu Mazen and the rumored legal proceedings against Sami, Iraq’s anti-corruption campaign is gaining traction among established political players.

However, the claims are still being examined, and individuals who are being arrested have the right to due process.

World.title: 'Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother': Vijay moves Tamil anthem resolution; DMK, AIADMK back it
World.content:
Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891. (Photo: PTI)

What does the resolution say?

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state.Moving the resolution in the state assembly, Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights and urged legislators to set aside political differences in supporting the measure."Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother," Vijay said in an emotive speech, adding that, "Tamil is not only a language but also our life and emotions.""Tamil means pride, Tamil means power. The moment you say 'Tamil', the entire Tamil Nadu will come together and stand as one," he said."Tamil Thai Vazhthu must hold the first place in Tamil Nadu. Giving first place to Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu is our state right," he noted."Saying that Tamil Thai Vazhthu should be sung first does not need to become a political debate," the Tamil nadu CM said, appealing to members across party lines to support the resolution.Under the resolution, Tamil Thai Vazhthu will be sung first at programmes held by educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings and other public institutions in Tamil Nadu.The resolution received support from both DMK and AIADMK legislators, with members backing the government's move to mandate the singing of the state song at official functions.The move comes amid a recent advisory from the Union home ministry asking states and Union territories to comply with its January 28 directive on playing Vande Mataram before the National Anthem at official events.It also comes against the backdrop of a July 9 communication from the ministry of home affairs regarding the singing of state songs at official programmes.The resolution describes Tamil Thai Vazhthu as an expression of respect for the Tamil language and culture and links its mandatory rendition to the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed under the Constitution."Therefore, this House ( Tamil Nadu Assembly ) emphasises that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" is an expression of respect for the Tamil language and Tamil culture. In accordance with the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India, and with a view to preserving the Cultural identity of Tamil Nadu, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly unanimously resolves that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" shall be mandatorily sung first, before the commencement of programmes held by all Educational Institutions, Universities, Government Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and other Public Institutions in Tamil Nadu," the resolution said.The resolution also notes that Tamil is one of the world's oldest classical languages and describes Tamil civilisation as one of the world's oldest cultural traditions.Tamil Nadu had first directed that Tamil Thai Vazhthu be sung at the beginning of official functions through a government order issued on November 23, 1970.The state government formally accorded the song the status of the state song on December 12, 2021, making its rendition mandatory at official programmes and institutions across the state.Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891.

World.title: Jharkhand assembly gherao: Security stepped up with 750m curbs, barbed-wire barricades
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ranchi is under heightened security on Monday as protesting students prepare to march to the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.

The students, who have been agitating for 16 days, have announced a âVidhan Sabha Marchâ despite the state government saying it has accepted 98 per cent of their demands.

March to begin at 10:30 am

The march is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium from 9 am, according to student leader Ravindra Paswan. He urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms.

Speaking to ANI, Paswan said, "A march to the Vidhan Sabha and a gherao will be conducted in a peaceful and constitutional manner.

Students started gathering there at 9:00 AM. The march will commence between 10:30 and 11:00 AM. I urge all students and the general public to maintain peace and adhere to constitutional norms. Since we students are leading this movement, we must demonstrate that we are disciplined and educated.

Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today's protest; there will be a massive turnout."

Prohibitory orders around Assembly

A prohibitory order has been imposed within a 750-metre radius of the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha from August 6 to 12.





The restrictions will remain in force from 6 am to 10 pm each day.

Barricades and barbed wire deployed

Police have put up barricades around the Assembly premises, with barbed wire installed at parts of the protest route to prevent demonstrators from reaching restricted areas.

Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyoneâs responsibility. "We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order.

Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.

Security stepped up across Ranchi

The Jharkhand Police and district administration have made elaborate security arrangements across the city ahead of the studentsâ âVidhan Sabha Marchâ. The government said no student would be harassed during the protest.

Schools to remain closed

Most schools in Ranchi will remain closed on Monday in view of the planned march, with authorities taking precautionary measures ahead of the expected turnout.

Ranchi administration warns against aggressive protests

The Ranchi district administration appealed to agitating students to refrain from aggressive demonstrations and cautioned against violence or illegal activities during the march to the Assembly.

BJP alleges Aditya Sahu placed under house arrest

BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged that the partyâs state unit president Aditya Sahu had been âput under house arrestâ ahead of Mondayâs protest.

World.title: To bypass Bosphorus & Hormuz, Russia moots direct rail link to India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Russian deputy PM Marat Khusnullin has suggested exploring a direct rail link from Moscow to the âIndian Oceanâ to avert risks associated with the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz, amid ongoing conflicts, including in West Asia, that have stalled the ambitious India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.

Bosphorus is a narrow, natural strait in Turkey that connects Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.

âA rail link to the Indian Ocean should also be explored. Risks related to the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz might require alternative routes: through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. Any options providing access to India are acceptable,â he told Russian news agency TASS.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Experts said constructing a rail link spanning two continents and four countries would be a gigantic challenge.

Apart from logistical difficulty and cost, for any option to extend the rail link to India, New Delhi would have to deal with the fact that it would pass through Pakistan, and a lot would depend on obtaining an iron-clad guarantee for securing cooperation and commitment of the hostile neighbour to protect the railway and cargo.

The statement does not provide a detailed construction plan, cost estimate or timeline. However, if such a corridor is eventually developed, it could create a direct overland rail freight route linking Russia with India while offering an alternative to traditional maritime shipping routes.

Among railway corridors linking multiple nations, Yiwu-Madrid is the longest freight train line in the world â spanning a little over 13,000 km, it connects Chinaâs Yiwu to Spainâs Madrid, traversing eight countries.

World.title: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The captain of Air Indiaâs August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight, which experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet, was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival, whose result was ânot negativeâ and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said Sunday.

TOI had exclusively reported on Sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.

The ministry has classified the incident, which led to 17 people being hospitalised, as serious and said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will probe it.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âFurther action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,â it said.

Air India pilots grounded till probe is over

Directorate General of Civil Aviation rules stipulate that âin case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety-sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received.

In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisationâ for de-addiction.

Multiple passengers and cabin crew members on board the Airbus A320 operating as AI 2379 were injured when it suddenly lost altitude. The plane later landed safely in Delhi. âAs standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing.

Samples have been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,â the ministry statement added.

Both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA, pending investigation.

World.title: Government may be going slow on FCRA to woo DMK, NCP(SP) for delimitation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The passage of FCRA amendment bill is not in Lok Sabha's agenda for Monday as Parliament's monsoon session enters its last week, giving rise to the view that government may be going slow on the contentious piece of legislation to sweeten the deal for parties such as

and NCP(SP), which are opposed to its provisions and are being seen by the governing alliance as prospective backers for its delimitation exercise.

Sources said the meeting of LS's business advisory committee, where upcoming agenda items are finalised, on Monday will give more clarity as a schedule for discussion on the bill should be fixed if it has to be taken up for passage in the remaining four days of Parliament's monsoon session ending on Aug 13. Monday's agenda includes the introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill.

Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill

The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.

Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments, saying it threatens their charitable works and will allow the government to seize their assets if their FCRA licence is withdrawn or not renewed.





What has, though, made things politically trickier for the BJP is the support extended by DMK president M K Stalin to the demand of a delegation representing churches of different denominations in their meeting with home minister Amit Shah that the bill be either withdrawn or sent to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.

With the government looking to assuage DMKâs concerns to get it on board before it makes a fresh bid for Parliamentâs nod for its delimitation exercise, coupled with implementation of the womenâs reservation law from 2029, it may not like to put the regional party on the defensive by bringing up the FCRA bill, some MPs said.

Supriya Sule of NCP SP, another party being eyed by the government as a probable supporter for the amendment bill, has also opposed the FCRA bill.

Mizoram CM Lalduhoma had told the media after joining a group of Church bodies from his state for a meeting with Amit Shah on Thursday that he was told that a debate on the bill is expected to be held on Aug 12.

The continuing impasse in Parliament due to the oppositionâs protests has added uncertainty as the government will prefer a full-fledged debate so that the home ministry could address the criticism around the bill.

World.title: Jharkhand students protest LIVE: Protestors break barricades, start marching towards Assembly
World.content:
The Jharkhand Police has imposed prohibitory orders around the assembly premises and made elaborate security arrangements across the city in view of Monday’s (August 10, 2026) ‘Vidhan Sabha March’ called by students who have been protesting for more than two weeks against irregularities in recruitment exams in the state. Protestors alleged that hundreds of students coming to the State capital from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by the police forcefully.

Also read: For Jharkhand’s Adivasi youth, competitive exams are about finding a voice in the system that governs them

The Jharkhand government on Sunday (August 9, 2026) agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination and the JPSC backlog examinations held in 2023 and 2025 following six hours of discussions with protesting student groups. However, the students remained firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination and said the agitation would continue. The announcement came even as all three JPSC members resigned and Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured protesters that “justice will be delivered with full transparency”.

Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) and JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, said they want cancellation of JSSC-CGL and all exams connected to the TSR Data Processing Private Limited Agency, a blacklisted entity.

Floor leaders of the Opposition parties will hold a meeting in the chamber of the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, to chalk out the strategy for the Floor of the House on Monday (August 10, 2026).

World.title: ‘Will pure petrol come from your father’s house’: BJP MP Janardan Mishra defends ethanol policy
World.content:
Amid the ongoing controversy over the blending of ethanol in petrol in the country, BJP MP from Rewa, Janardan Mishra, on Sunday (August 9, 2026) defended the Centre’s ethanol policy and asked its opponents, “Will pure petrol come from your father's house?”

Also read | The legal questions surrounding India’s E20 rollout | Explained

Addressing an event to inaugurate new flight services from Rewa to Bhopal and Kolkata, Mr. Mishra said that India produces only 20% of crude oil, while 80% has to be imported from abroad.

Citing the global geopolitical situation, the BJP MP claimed that ships have to travel an additional distance of approximately 18,000 k.m. to supply oil.

“In such a situation, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi talks about blending 20% ethanol in petrol, some people start protesting.”

“A movement is underway claiming that ethanol won't work, pure petrol will. Will pure petrol come from your father's house? If there's no pure petrol in the country, where will it come from?" he said.

Mr. Mishra also said that vehicles in India can run on ethanol blending, but some people are saying don’t use it.

“If ethanol is not produced, where will petrol come from, where will diesel come from?”

Defending ethanol blending in petrol, he claimed that in Brazil, vehicles run on 100% ethanol, and there are no problems with vehicles there.

Brazil produces maximum ethanol in the world, which is why vehicles there run on 100% ethanol, he said.

Mr. Mishra, who often makes headlines for his controversial comments, said that experts in India also believe that ethanol does not harm vehicle engines, yet there is “unnecessary” opposition to it.

He also claimed that if there is any place in the world today where inflation is the lowest and employment is highest, it is in India.

World.title: Orthodox, Jacobite priests and members clash at church in Kerala
World.content:
Priests and members of the Orthodox and Jacobite factions of the Malankara Church clashed at St. John’s Bethlehem Church in Piramadom, near Muvattupuzha, on Sunday (August 9).

The clash erupted after members and priests of the Orthodox faction allegedly arrived at the church, claiming to have obtained a favourable court order regarding its ownership. The church was under the control of the Jacobite faction, the police said.

The Holy Mass led by a Jacobite priest was reportedly under way when members of the rival faction arrived with the court order. The police dispersed members of both factions to de-escalate the situation and temporarily locked the church as a preventive measure. Visuals showing priests from both factions pushing and shoving each other near the altar, while members of the factions intervened, were widely shared on social media.

Meanwhile, the district administration is expected to hold discussions with representatives of both factions on Monday (August 10).

World.title: Assam flood situation critical; death toll reaches 100, nearly 1.4 lakh affected
World.content:
The flood situation in Assam remained critical on Monday (August 11, 2026) as the toll touched 100 with two more deaths, while almost 1.4 lakh people reel under the deluge in seven districts, according to an official bulletin.

An official of the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said several rivers are flowing above their danger mark, posing a threat to newer areas.

According to the authority’s daily flood bulletin on Sunday night (August 10, 2026), two persons have lost their lives in the deluge in Golaghat and Karbi Anglong districts in 24 hours.

With these fatalities, the total number of deaths in this year’s floods has increased to 100.

At present, 456 villages are inundated, while 11,933.46 hectares of crop areas have been damaged across Assam.

According to ASDMA’s daily flood report, more than 1,37,500 people have been affected in Charaideo, Darrang, Golaghat, Jorhat, Karbi Anglong, Nagaon and Sivasagar districts.

Golaghat is the worst-hit, with almost 70,000 people affected, followed by Sivasagar with nearly 40,000 people and Jorhat with more than 16,000 people reeling under floodwaters.

An ASDMA official said that the Dhansiri river at Golaghat and Numaligarh and the Kushiyara river at Sribhumi are flowing above the danger level. “Due to a steady rise in the water level of Dhansiri in Golaghat district, people have been advised to stay away from the river,” she added.

ASDMA said that the administration has been operating 125 relief camps and relief distribution centres in six districts, taking care of 49,061 people at present.

World.title: This app is dropping curated mystery bags from your favourite cafes in Bengaluru
World.content:
Ever been stuck doom scrolling Swiggy because you cannot decide what to eat? Thanks to food delivery apps, we are spoilt for choice — a little too much one might say. Start-up founder Akshay Bhartiya is solving this problem with his new app called Luckd. With this food delivery app, you do not have to select the dishes you want. They deliver surprise mystery bags from popular cafes and restaurants in the city. Here is how it works.

“When I lived in the UK, we had fewer options for delivery, but it was more curated. In India we are bombarded with too many options. What we are building is a marketplace for curated experiences. We are streamlining the options. Think of us like a FirstClub for experiences,“ says Akshay who has an engineering background, and did his MBA from Esade Business School in Barcelona.

Luckd has tied up with bakeries in the HSR Layout and Koramangala area. Users can download the app, and login with their phone number and add their addresses. The app has drops throughout the day, such as breakfast, coffee, or lunch time. Bakeries list their best sellers, or sometimes a chef’s special in these drops. Users cannot see the exact dishes that are in the bag, but details such as allergens and dietary preferences are listed. They are priced around ₹300-₹350. After ordering, the food is delivered to your doorstep in 30 minutes or so. The bag will have a surprise mix of goodies from the cafe.

Luckd has an in-house curator, and has tied up with smaller hidden gems as well as big name popular bakeries. Some cafes you can find on the app are Glen’s Bakehouse, The Humble Pie, Crave Theory and Mary Janes Bakery & Deli. Luckd also has options such as Salad Street Co and Poiee (a restaurant specialising in Goan poee sandwiches).

“We have our own rider fleet. We have delivery drivers on our payroll, and some sourced from a third-party.” To begin with, the app is only available for deliveries in limited areas of the city but looking to expand to Whitefield and Indiranagar. Food safety and quality is a priority for Akshay.

The app is bootstrapped now, and Akshay says he is seeing a lot of retention and repeat customers. The supply is outweighing the demand, so they are building on curating more restaurants. “For people like us who are busy and managing so many other things, we need a smaller number of options. It is like a treat to you every day.” In the future, Luckd wants to move beyond food, and venture into beauty, wellness and outdoor experiences.

Luckd is available on the App Store and Google Play

World.title: Kanwar Yatra 2026: Traffic restrictions in Delhi, U.P., and Haryana

Delhi CM assures kanwariyas will not face any difficulties

TRAFFIC ADVISORY



Traffic movement in and around Kalindi Kunj Junction is likely to remain slow and congested till 12.08.2026 due to heavy movement of Kanwariyas during the ongoing Kanwar Yatra and ongoing road repair work on the Okhla Barrage–Kalindi Kunj stretch.



📍ADVISORY… pic.twitter.com/dzqYI092mO — Delhi Traffic Police (@dtptraffic) August 9, 2026

Gurugram, Haryana

Gurugram traffic police, on August 8, detailed alternate routes for heavy vehicles to take to enter the national capital of Delhi owing to the ‘Kanwar Yatra’ pilgrimage and the return of the ‘kanwariyas’ from Haridwar.

School van vandalised in Lucknow allegedly by Kanwariyas

It asked commuters to “use Dwarka and KMP expressway via Panchgaon Chowk” as travel corridors to Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and Faridabad may also be affected.

This advisory is in effect till August 11, 2026 and the traffic police also attached maps for easy referencing for citizens.

Heavy Vehicle Advisory (9–11 Aug)

Kanwariyas return from Haridwar for jalabhishek on Mahashivratri, 11 Aug.

· Use Dwarka & KMP Expressway via Panchgaon Chowk

· For Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, Faridabad

📞 112 | 1095#TrafficAdvisory#KMPExpressway#RoadSafetypic.twitter.com/QNABiSDIuF — Gurugram Traffic Police (@TrafficGGM) August 8, 2026

Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh

Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh is also under a traffic advisory by the traffic police. An X post, with a video by Varun Kumar Singh, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic), said that “For the safe movement of Kanwar devotees, the Delhi-Meerut Expressway (DME) will be restricted for general traffic on August 10 and 11, 2026.” It added that: In view of the large number of Kanwar pilgrims on NH-58/Delhi-Meerut route, use Rapid Metro (RRTS) and public transport instead of private vehicles, and use NH-09 as much as possible.

Traffic curbs for Kanwar Yatra in U.P.’s Muzaffarnagar till August 12

Vehicles coming from Siddharth Vihar to Meerut Tiraha should use NH-09, Vijayanagar Cut, Overbridge, and Chaudhary Mod.”

It advised locals to use NH-09 instead for commuting.

What is Kanwar Yatra?

Kanwar Yatra is an annual pilgrimage where devotees of Lord Shiva collect holy water from the Ganges River from places like Haridawar, Gangotri, Gaumukh, or Sultanganj and take it to their local temples, often walking barefoot for long distances.

It occurs during July-August, depending on the Hindu calendar month of ‘Shravan.’

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran ties Strait of Hormuz reopening to U.S. concessions on several demands
World.content:
Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman to define new shipping lanes between them through the Strait of Hormuz, but reiterated that the U.S. must meet other conditions, including compensation and an end to sanctions and military threats, before the strategic waterway is reopened.

Also read | Mecca Agreement | A new triple alliance in West Asia

A U.S. official told Reuters on August 7, 2026, that Iran and Oman were close to a deal that ⁠could pave the way for restoring safe passage through the strait, a major conduit for oil and gas shipping before Iran blocked Hormuz in response to U.S. and Israeli attacks on Tehran that began in late February.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi said on August 9, 2026, that an agreement with Oman on the strait was in its “final stages,” but reiterated comments made on August 8 that Tehran would not reopen the channel unless the U.S. met certain demands.

Also read | A new security triangle emerges with the Makkah Pact

Iran and the U.S. are not engaged in direct talks, and Tehran will not start them ⁠as long as Washington breaches an interim deal signed in June, Mr. Aragchi said, adding that messages were being exchanged through intermediaries.

World.title: 3rd phase of AJK polls: Voting underway in Poonch Division's Bagh and Haveli districts
World.content:
The third phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) is currently underway in four constituencies in Poonch Division’s Bagh and Haveli districts. Polling began at 8am and will continue until 5pm.

Government officials have anticipated clashes in some areas, while the Election Commission has classified most of the 803 polling stations in the four constituencies as either sensitive or highly sensitive.

“Apart from the regular police of both districts, we have dispatched an additional 10,300 troops to maintain law and order and provide a fear-free atmosphere to voters,” Election Commission Secretary Raja Mohammad Shakeel told Dawn earlier.

Elections are being held across AJK in phases amid tensions between protesters and the authorities. Polling in Mirpur and Muzaff­arabad divisions was held on July 27 and Aug 2, respectively, with the PML-N securing 24 seats. The PPP has only secured 10 seats so far.

The third phase of the polls was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division. The division comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.

However, last week the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli due to concerns over the law and order situation. The AJK election commissioner has hinted that polling on the remaining seven constituencies could be held by Aug 20 or 21.

Rathore, two ex-AJK PMs face crucial electoral test

AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore and two of his predecessors — Sardar Tanveer Ilyas and Sardar Attique Ahmed Khan — face a battle for political survival as voters head to the polls.

Around 238,664 men and 221,707 women are eligible to cast their ballots at 803 polling stations comprising 1,254 polling booths.

A total of 82 candidates are in the fray, with LA-14 (Dhirkot) attracting the highest number of candidates at 30 and LA-17 (Haveli) the lowest at nine.

In LA-17, Rathore is facing PML-N candidate Engr Mohsin Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed, a member of the AJK Council.

Rathore and Saeed had been political allies and, under an agreement, had agreed to contest the seat alternately. However, after becoming prime minister, Rathore asked Saeed to step aside in his favour, a request he did not accept, turning the former allies into rivals.

Aziz, whose father, Chaudhry Mohammad Aziz, had won the seat at least three times, draws support from the sizeable Gujjar community. His recent large election rally in Forward Kahuta reportedly surprised his rivals and underscored the strength of his campaign.

Saeed, meanwhile, is believed to enjoy the backing of a sizeable section of the Kashmiri community, as well as an alliance of several smaller clans.

Rathore, however, remains confident of retaining the seat, citing the performance of his government during his relatively brief tenure as prime minister.

The constituency has also witnessed allegations of electoral irregularities on social media, with reports claiming that two presiding officers had been caught manipulating results in favour of Rathore. Shakeel dismissed the allegations but at the same time confirmed that complaints had been received against the two officials and that they had subsequently been relieved of election duties.

In LA-15 (Wasti Bagh), former prime minister Ilyas is facing PML-N candidate and former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas, PPP nominee and sitting minister Sardar Ziaul Qamar, and Jamaat-i-Islami candidate retired Brig Dr Mohammad Khan, a respected educationist.

Ilyas, who secured a little over 3,300 votes from Upper Neelum in the second phase of the elections, had initially announced a boycott of the third phase. He subsequently reversed the decision and resumed campaigning, claiming that his victory would enable the constituency to “secure either the presidency or prime ministership.”

Ilyas and Qamar belong to the same Madiyal tribe, while Brig Khan belongs to the Narma clan and enjoys the support of former JI chief Abdul Rashid Turabi and former adviser Raja Yasin Khan.

Minhas has the advantage of belonging to the PML-N, which is poised to form the next government after emerging as the largest party in the elections held so far. His campaign has also stressed the argument that voters should elect a candidate from the party that is set to occupy the government benches rather than send their representative to the opposition.

In LA-16 (Sharqi Bagh), former ministers Sardar Mir Akbar and Sardar Qamar Zaman are the principal contenders, representing the PML-N and PPP, respectively.

The fourth contest, LA-14 (Dhirkot), has drawn particular attention because of the challenge faced by Sardar Attique, head of the once-dominant Muslim Conference (MC).

Attique is reportedly facing a strong challenge from Sajid Iqbal Abbasi of the relatively new Awam Dast-o-Bazu Party. A contractor and philanthropist, Abbasi is said to have spent millions of rupees from his own resources on public welfare projects in the constituency, helping him build a sizeable personal following.

Attique, who has represented the constituency successively since 2006, when he first became prime minister, faces an additional challenge in that Abbasi also belongs to the same tribe.

Among nearly two dozen other candidates are PML-N’s nominee Raja Faisal Azad and PPP candidate Raja Mubashar Ejaz. While the main contest is seen as being between Attique and Abbasi, the PML-N and PPP nominees are expected to vie for the second runner-up position.

World.title: Rs115bn WB-funded rehabilitation project restructured quietly
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Amid a blame game and fiduciary concerns, the government has quietly restructured the Rs115 billion World Bank-funded post-flood rehabilitation project, depriving more than 134,000 verified flood-affected families in Balochistan of the resilient homes they were promised.

Official documents and background discussions indicate that investigations were underway into alleged record tampering, duplicate claims and multiple payments for the same housing units. There were also recorded attempts to disrupt such probes.

The project steering committee (PSC), led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, has now capped the $155 million housing component of the $400m Integrated Flood Resilience & Adaptation Project (IFRAP) at about 69,000 homes. The World Bank has consequently dropped its proposed $180m additional financing that could have extended reconstruction to the remaining affected families.

After the devastating 2022 floods, Pakistan secured more than $9bn in international pledges at the January 2023 Geneva Conference. IFRAP was designed to rebuild homes in Balochistan through a community-led, owner-driven model. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had publicly promised a resilient house for every family that lost one. Yet at its June 22-23 meeting, the PSC unanimously redirected the remaining housing funds towards roads and irrigation and formally declined additional World Bank financing.

Over 134,000 flood-hit families in Balochistan being affected amid investigations of record tampering, duplicate claims

The decision reverses that commitment, despite more than 134,000 verified families having been surveyed and registered for assistance.

PSC meeting minutes showed the planning minister expressed concern over “misreporting” of completed houses as “the number of completed houses presented to the Prime Minister was 15,000 whereas official reports reflected 8,694 completed houses”.

There are conflicting arguments – one side claiming misreporting to downgrade housing project for ‘redirecting’ funds to contractor-oriented larger infrastructure project and the other side showing concern over slow pace of house completion in four years due to lack of land titles, access to financial accounts and transparency. The planning commission has now proposed satellite imagery for verification.

Both the minister and the CM ordered an independent high-level inquiry to ensure transparency and accountability. The committee also noted serious corruption charges against certain officials but the fact finding committee could not be given access to records in Balochistan.

Not only this, the ministries of planning and economic affairs appeared at different wavelength. The EAD put on record that the WB had expressed concerns over changes in project leadership arrangements. Clearly, the bank and the planning commission apparently had their own priorities for the project leadership.

Informed source said the minister for planning and WB country director Bolormaa Amgaabazar have had at least two meetings to clear the situation but issues continue to prolong.

Interestingly, a similar project, the Sindh People’s Housing for Flood Affectees (SPHF) involving around $3bn funding and over 2m home reconstructions, goes on and presents a success story though the planning commission remains unhappy without a third-party verification.

When contacted, the commission said the inclusive development programme “under IFRAP was damaged in a coordinated manner for vested interests by shifting financing from important sectors i.e. education, health, PHE, irrigation, bridges, roads, livelihood and youth skill development to housing to show burn rate”.

The commission denied that housing project had been stopped, adding that about 75,000 fully damaged houses were under construction, 26,000 of them completed. It said the project originally approved by Ecnec was 68,922 that would remain protected. It said vested interests planned diversion of funds from early warning system, irrigation etc to housing in violation of Ecnec approved scope. It reported that out of total $400m IFRAP envelope, $245m had already been signed.

It said the allegation of misreporting of 15,000 completed houses to PM was raised by a local parliamentarian, and inquiry established misrepresentation.

About different treatments to two similar projects in Sindh and Balochistan, the commission said they were incomparable, as IFRAP in Balochistan was a federal budget project with a single WB loan on federal government and involved budgetary disbursement and compliance requirements while Sindh was a direct borrower from multiple lenders and financed through section 42 entity – a non-profit non-binding disbursement schedules.

World.title: High court judge to investigate Mir Raza murder case, says home minister
World.content:
• Announcement comes hours after Faryal Talpur recommends judicial probe

• Previous investigation body sent packing as IGP forms new team

• DSP, Jauhar SHO suspended for failing to preserve crime scene

• Sharjeel moves NCCIA over ‘defamatory campaign’

KARACHI: In what appears to be a damage-control exercise, the provincial government has decided to conduct a judicial inquiry by a judge of the Sindh High Court into the murder of young businessman Mir Raza Ali, a day after a fresh autopsy ruled out the possibility of suicide on the grounds that he had been shot in the back and that his body bore marks of torture.

An announcement to this effect was made by Sindh Home Minister Zia Lanjar a few hours after senior Pakistan Peoples Party leader and chairperson of the Sindh Assembly’s Standing Committee on Home Affairs, Faryal Talpur, recommended that the chief minister constitute a judicial commission to conduct a transparent, impartial and comprehensive investigation into the case.

An IBA graduate and owner of the eatery Wafflix, Mir Raza had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-i-Jauhar.

When investigators reportedly focused their probe on the possibility of suicide and reports emerged about a flawed autopsy, Raza’s family filed an application before a judicial magistrate seeking the exhumation of the body for a fresh post-mortem examination.

While the magistrate ordered the exhumation, the provincial government changed the composition of the medical board three times, fuelling rumours that there was an attempt to cover up the case. Later, the government restored the original medical board that had carried out the exhumation and conducted the autopsy and found that he had suffered injuries and had been shot in the back.

On Sunday, in an attempt to show the public that there’s nothing to hide, senior PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light.

“Legal and disciplinary action should be taken without discrimination against those found responsible in light of the commission’s findings,” she added.

Talpur stressed that justice for the victim’s family must be ensured at all costs and that the public should be transparently informed of all facts surrounding the case.

“No negligence or bias will be tolerated in meeting the requirements of justice,” she said, adding that providing justice to the bereaved family and maintaining public confidence in the justice system were fundamental responsibilities of the government and relevant institutions.

A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Home Minister Lanjar and Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab reached deceased Raza’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice.

Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case.

He said a transparent and impartial investigation would be ensured.

Speaking on the occasion, Mayor Wahab noted that Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah chaired a four-hour-long meeting during which “all aspects of the incident and the investigation were reviewed in detail”.

New investigation team formed

The Sindh police chief dismissed the previous investigation team headed by Special Investigation Unit SSP Dr Samiullah Soomro and appointed DIG Amir Farooqi to lead a five-member new committee.

Other members of the committee are SSP Syed Muhammad Ali Raza, SP Qais Khan, SP Anam Tajjamul and Inspector Ch. Ghazanfar.

According to a notification, “The team shall undertake a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the case from all relevant angles. The team shall identify, collect, preserve and examine any new or additional evidence and shall thoroughly examine and analyse all physical, technical, circumstantial and forensic evidence collected during the investigation.

“The team shall make all-out efforts to work out the case and submit a report to the court concerned within the stipulated period. The team may co-opt any officer to assist in the investigation. Progress shall be reported on a day-to-day basis,” it added.

DSP, Jauhar SHO suspended

Karachi police chief Azad Khan has suspended Sharea Faisal DSP Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar SHO Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect.

A police spokesperson said that both officials were suspended for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after the body of Mir Raza was found.

Sharjeel moves NCCIA against ‘malicious social media campaign’

Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon, through his counsel, filed an application before the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) against unknown persons for “causing harassment, creating false and malicious content on social media against him and his son.

The application stated that certain social media accounts began circulating posts, videos and statements against Memon and his son, containing “allegations that are false, baseless, fabricated, and malicious in nature, and which are calculated to injure their reputation, dignity, and standing in society”.

Memon stated that none of the allegations — that he owned the guest house in Gulistan-i-Jauhar, where Mir Raza was allegedly tortured and murdered and that his son had left for London immediately after the incident and has since been moving around with a bodyguard — has “any factual or evidentiary basis, and each is false, baseless, and malicious, being designed solely to malign” him and his son for extraneous political motives.

His lawyer asked the NCCIA to register an FIR and proceed in accordance with law against the persons found responsible under the applicable provisions of the Prevention of Electronic Crime Act 2016 and any other law found attracted.

World.title: Tarbela Dam attains maximum storage level
World.content:
LAHORE: Tarbela Dam, the country’s second largest reservoir after Mangla Dam, reached its maximum storage level of 1,550-feet on Sunday, reflecting a significant increase in the country’s water conservation capacity.

Sources attribute the filling of the Tarbela Dam to the ongoing high-flow season due to rains and snow melting.

According to the flood forecasting division of the Pakistan Meteorological Department, the water conservation level in the dam at 6pm on Sunday reached 1,549.48 feet after increasing from 1,549 feet gauged at 6am.

The minimum operating/dead level of the dam is 1,402 feet and the live storage recorded on Sunday was 5.523 Million-Acre Feet (MAF).

In 2024 and 2025 (same day), Tarbela Dam had attained filling to 90pc and 96pc, respectively. On the other hand, the water conservation/storage level in Mangla Dam is also increasing fast and reached 1,206.45 feet, around 35.50 feet short of its full storage capacity of 1,242 feet. Since the minimum operating level of the dam is 1,050 feet, the live storage recorded on Sunday remained at 4.621 MAF.

Last year, Tarbela attained its maximum storage level on August 21, followed by Chashma Lake that also attained its maximum level of 649 feet. At present, Chashma Lake has almost achieved its maximum conservation level of 649 feet, as its current storage level is 648.50 feet. Since the minimum operating level of the lake is 638.15 feet, the live storage remained 0.285 MAF.

Meanwhile, the FFD says no significant increase in inflows is expected at major gauging stations of Rivers Indus, Kabul, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi and Sutlej over the next 24 hours, although low-level flood conditions are likely to persist at several barrages on the Indus.

The flows at the Kalabagh, Chashma, Taunsa and Guddu barrages on the Indus are expected to remain at low flood levels whereas an increase in flows is also likely in hill torrents in northern Balochistan and Dera Ghazi Khan division.

The FFD predicts urban flooding in Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Sialkot, Narowal, Faisalabad, Okara and Lahore amid the prevailing weather conditions.

It also expects a fresh spell of rains from Aug 10 (today) in Islamabad, Kashmir, Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and upper Punjab. The fresh spell may also trigger an increase in flows in streams and nullahs adjoining upper catchments of rivers and key river-gauging stations, according to the forecast.

Authorities have been advised to remain alert due to possible rises in water levels in vulnerable areas as the new weather system develops.

According to a daily report of the Water and Power Authority (Wapda), the inflows and outflows at River Indus at Tarbela were 205,700 cusecs and 175,900 cusecs, respectively, followed by the River Kabul having Inflows of 4000 cusecs and outflows of 4000 cusecs at Noshehra.

The inflows and outflows at Jhelum River at Mangla were 31,700 cusecs and 7,000 cusecs, respectively, followed by the River Chenab having inflows of 65,000 cusecs and outflows of 45,000 cusecs at Marala headworks.

“The inflows and outflows of the River Indus at Tarbela, Jinnah and Chashma, River Kabul at Nowshera and River Jhelum at Mangla have been reflected as mean flows of 24 hours, whereas other flows were gauged at 6am,” the Wapda report says.

World.title: AJK govt appoints Public Service Commission members amid questions over timing
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Days before its exit from power, the incumbent Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) government has appointed seven members to Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s (AJK) Public Service Commission (PSC), the top recruitment body of AJK, a move that has raised questions about its propriety and timing.

According to a notification issued by the Services and General Administration Department, the appointments were made by the government in exercise of the powers conferred under Article 48(2) of the AJK Interim Constitution, 1974, read with Section 4(3) of the AJK Public Service Commission Act, 1986.

Those appointed include former secretaries Munir Hussain Chaudhary, Dr Chaudhry Liaqat Hussain and Mohammad Zahid Abbasi from the quota of retired government servants in BS-20 and above; former professor Dr Abdul Qadoos Khan and former vice chancellor Dr Abdul Hameed from the quota of educationists; former additional chief secretary Midhat Shehzad from the quota of women; and retired medical specialist Dr Mohammad Saleem Khan from the quota of professionals.

Under the Public Service Commission Act, seven members are to be appointed from among retired civil servants or other outstanding persons with a good reputation and an educational qualification of at least graduation from a recognised university. Three members are to be appointed from among educationists or scholars having a good reputation and at least 10 years’ experience in teaching, administration or both.

PML-N takes strong exception to move by outgoing PPP govt

The new members will have a three-year term and will be entitled to draw pay and allowances as prescribed, the notification said. It added that their appointments would take effect from the date they took oath of their respective offices in terms of Section 4-A of the AJK Public Service Commission Act, 1986.

Shahid Mehmood Wani, a senior PML-N leader who was also a member of the party’s election manifesto committee, took strong exception to what he described as the questionable propriety and timing of the appointments.

“Without questioning the competence or credentials of the individuals appointed, the propriety of making such appointments at this stage is certainly open to question. A government continuing in office as a transitional arrangement after the expiry of the assembly’s term, and having lost the people’s mandate, should ordinarily leave decisions of such long-term institutional consequence to the incoming elected government,” he said.

The AJK Public Service Commission has long faced criticism over delays in its constitution and allegations that its members are appointed on the basis of the preferences of the government of the day rather than through a transparent process.

In May 2023, when the three-year term of chairman retired Air Marshal Masood Akhtar and those of the commission’s members expired, the body was left without a complete composition for the next eight months.

The latest appointments come as the PPP government continues in office after the expiry of the AJK Legislative Assembly’s constitutional term of five years, pending completion of the election process. The PPP has also lost its majority in the elections held so far, with the PML-N emerging as the largest party and poised to form the next government.

World.title: Judicial probe launched into death of 2 girls in Lahore police custody
World.content:
LAHORE: A judicial magistrate has initiated an inquiry under Section 176 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) into the suspicious death of two underage girls in Lahore police custody on Aug 4, as mystery continues to surround the horrific, tragic incident.

The judicial inquiry was launched after the families of the victims – Amina and Anmol – demanded an impartial investigation into what happened to the girls in the police custody for well over two hours – from the time of their arrest to calling a Rescue 1122 team to the Township police station on Aug 4.

Section 176 of the CrPC empowers a magistrate to inquire into the cause of death when a person dies in police custody or under some suspicious circumstances. The law also empowers the magistrate to order exhumation of a body for the postmortem examination, besides recording statements and examining witnesses on oath.

Dawn spoke to police officers familiar with the matter and attempted to map the sequence of events from the girls’ arrest to their deaths.

According to an official, around 2:54pm on Aug 4 an emergency call was received on police helpline 15 from complainant, Zeshan Latif, who alleged that two girls entered his house and fraudulently stole gold jewellery and cash belonging to his wife.

A sub-inspector (SI) of the Township police, Ghulam Ghous, reached the scene at 3:11pm and brought the two girls to the police station, where they were handed over to the duty clerk (Muharrar), Tasnim Arif, at 3:26pm.

Mr Latif subsequently submitted an application, which was e-tagged at 4:40pm, and an FIR was registered at 4:50pm against the two girls.

The Township police station then recorded a report at 5:20pm regarding the transfer of the girls’ custody from the operations wing to the investigation staff.

According to the official, the operations wing’s muharrar claimed that, following registration of the FIR, he handed over the girls to the investigation wing Muharrar Bilal, in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The situation took a grim turn shortly afterwards when, at 6:03pm, the central office of Rescue 1122 received an emergency call from the Township police regarding the deteriorating condition of both girls.

A Rescue 1122 team reached the police station at 6:14pm and found one of the girls “almost dead”, while the other was unconscious, according to the official.

Both were shifted to Jinnah Hospital, where doctors pronounced the unconscious girl dead. The other girl, who was reportedly in critical condition, also died shortly after in the hospital.

As news of the girls’ death spread, senior police officers from the Saddar Division’s operations and investigation wings reached the Township police station at around 9:30pm and sensing gravity of the situation apprised higher authorities about the incident.

The official says that incident triggered a row between the operations and investigation wings, with officers from both sides reportedly shifting the responsibility for the girls’ custody onto each other.

The time between 3:11pm, when the girls were taken into custody, and 6:03pm, when Rescue 1122 was called, is therefore crucial in the judicial inquiry, he adds.

Video footage that surfaced after the incident shows the girls apparently in a relatively stable condition when they were brought to the police station. In one recording, a police official can be seen questioning them.

Another video recorded by a camera installed in the duty clerk’s room shows Amina and Anmol sitting on chairs inside the police station. They appear conscious and are seen interacting with the duty clerk before leaving the room.

Police officials, however, say that details of the girls’ interaction and interrogation are not covered by the station’s security cameras.

Immediately after the incident, the investigation police claimed that drug overdose was the likely cause of the girls’ death. The claim, however, has yet to be conclusively established through the postmortem reports, which are crucial evidence in determining the death cause.

Police were still awaiting the final postmortem reports when Dawn spoke to officials.

Investigation SSP Mohammad Naveed strongly rejected allegations that the girls had been tortured in custody.

“Though I am not aware whether the final postmortem reports have been issued, I can assure you that the allegations of custodial torture are absolutely false and misleading,” he claimed.

The SSP alleges that both girls were chronic drug users and had apparently consumed a strong addictive substance before being brought to the police station. “During their custody at the police station, they fainted, probably because of the impact of the drugs they had consumed, and later died of the same cause,” he claimed.

Mr Naveed maintains that as a major portion of the girls interrogation had been captured by surveillance cameras installed at the police station, it shows girls were not maltreated in custody.

He says the judicial inquiry had been initiated at the request of senior police officers under Section 176 of the CrPC and that its findings would bring out the circumstances of the deaths.

Asked why the case had not been referred to the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), the SSP said the agency is usually asked to investigate the cases involving allegations that a suspect had died as a result of custodial torture or killed in a police encounter. “This case is different, as it concerns the deaths of two suspects in custody, and there was no need for an FIA investigation,” he insisted.

The judicial inquiry is expected to examine the circumstances surrounding the girls’ detention, the transfer of their custody between the operations and investigation wings, the available CCTV footage, statements of police officials and witnesses, and the postmortem reports’ findings to dig out the facts.

World.title: Former US president Joe Biden’s cancer has spread: son
World.content:
WASHINGTON: Former US president Joe Biden’s cancer has metastasised further, according to his son Hunter Biden, who shared the update in a recent interview with the BBC. In May 2025, just four months after he left office as the oldest sitting president, the elder Biden revealed he had been diagno­sed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones.

He subsequently began treatment, including radiation and hormone therapy, which the 83-year-old described as going “really well” last month, during an announcement of his upcoming memoir.

In a wide-ranging interview published late Friday with BBC Newsnight, Hunter Biden said his father’s disease has spread despite the treatment. “The cancer has spread, is metastasised into his bones and further,” Biden said.

“It’s very painful, and it’s very debilitating in many respects, but he’s still out there. He’s still doing his thing…he so believes in this country.” Hunter Biden appeared to get emotional at times during the interview while discussing his father’s health.
